nodes.summary: A binomial min-heap over a linearly ordered type $\alpha$ consists of a list of binomial trees over $\alpha$ together with a proof that this list is a valid binomial forest: every tree in it is a valid binomial tree and the tree ranks are strictly increasing along the list.
nodes.title: Binomial heap

nodes.summary: A binomial tree over a type $\alpha$ is a node that stores a rank, which is a natural number, a root value in $\alpha$, and a list of binomial trees over $\alpha$ as its children. The type imposes no invariant; the binomial-tree shape and heap order are expressed by a separate validity predicate.
nodes.title: Binomial tree

nodes.summary: For a type $\alpha$ with a relation $\le$, every valid binomial tree of rank $r$ over $\alpha$ represents a multiset of exactly $2^r$ elements, counted with multiplicity.
nodes.title: Size of a valid binomial tree

nodes.summary: For a linearly ordered type, the carry of a binomial tree $t$ into a list $F$ of binomial trees is defined by recursion on $F$. If $F$ is empty, the result is the one-tree list $[t]$. If $F$ starts with a tree $u$ followed by a list $F'$ and the rank of $t$ is less than the rank of $u$, the result is $F$ with $t$ prepended. Otherwise the result is the carry of the link of $t$ and $u$ into $F'$.
nodes.title: Carry insertion into a binomial forest

nodes.summary: For a type $\alpha$ with a relation $\le$, every child of a valid binomial tree over $\alpha$ is itself a valid binomial tree.
nodes.title: Children of a valid binomial tree are valid

nodes.summary: For a type $\alpha$ with a relation $\le$, if a valid binomial tree over $\alpha$ has rank $r$, then the ranks of its children, listed in their stored order, are $r - 1, r - 2, \dots, 1, 0$; there are no children when $r = 0$.
nodes.title: Child ranks of a valid binomial tree

nodes.summary: The children of a binomial tree are the binomial trees in the list stored at its root node, in their stored order.
nodes.title: Children of a binomial tree

nodes.summary: For a binomial heap $H$ over a linearly ordered type, if deleting the minimum of $H$ succeeds and returns a value $m$ and a heap $H'$, then the multiset of elements of $H$ equals the multiset of elements of $H'$ with one more occurrence of $m$.
nodes.title: Deleting the minimum of a binomial heap splits its multiset

nodes.summary: For a binomial heap $H$ over a linearly ordered type, if deleting the minimum of $H$ succeeds and returns a value $m$ and a heap $H'$, then the multiset of elements of $H'$ is the multiset of elements of $H$ with one occurrence of $m$ removed.
nodes.title: Deleting the minimum of a binomial heap removes one occurrence

nodes.summary: For a binomial heap $H$ over a linearly ordered type, deleting the minimum of $H$ returns no result if and only if the list of trees of $H$ is empty.
nodes.title: Deleting the minimum fails only on the empty binomial heap

nodes.summary: If deleting the minimum of a binomial heap $H$ over a linearly ordered type succeeds and returns a value $m$ together with a remaining heap, then $m \le v$ for every value $v$ in the multiset of elements of $H$.
nodes.title: The value deleted from a binomial heap is a lower bound for its elements

nodes.summary: For every binomial heap $H$ over a linearly ordered type, deleting the minimum of $H$ and then replacing the remaining heap by its list of trees gives the same result as minimum deletion on the list of trees of $H$: both have no result, or both return the same minimum value and the same list of trees.
nodes.title: Binomial heap deletion agrees with forest deletion

nodes.summary: Given a list of binomial trees over a linearly ordered type, if the list is empty there is no result. Otherwise, remove the first tree whose root is minimal among the roots of the list; the result is the root of that tree together with the forest obtained by melding its children, in reversed order, with the remaining trees.
nodes.title: Minimum deletion on a binomial forest

nodes.summary: If the binomial heap $H$ has no trees, there is no result. Otherwise, remove from the list of trees of $H$ the first tree whose root is minimal; the result is that root together with the binomial heap whose list of trees is obtained by melding the children of the removed tree, in reversed order, with the remaining trees.
nodes.title: Deleting the minimum of a binomial heap

nodes.summary: The multiset of elements of a list of binomial trees $t_1, \dots, t_k$ is the multiset sum of the multisets of elements of $t_1, \dots, t_k$; for the empty list it is the empty multiset.
nodes.title: Elements of a binomial forest

nodes.summary: Over a linearly ordered type, the multiset of elements of a binomial heap is the multiset of elements of its list of binomial trees, that is, the multiset sum of the multisets of elements of its trees.
nodes.title: Elements of a binomial heap

nodes.summary: For every binomial heap $H$ over a linearly ordered type and every value $v$, the multiset of elements of the heap obtained by inserting $v$ into $H$ is the multiset of elements of $H$ with one more occurrence of $v$.
nodes.title: Insertion into a binomial heap adds one occurrence

nodes.summary: For any two binomial trees $s$ and $t$ over a linearly ordered type, the multiset of elements of the tree obtained by linking $s$ and $t$ is the sum of the multisets of elements of $s$ and $t$.
nodes.title: Linking binomial trees adds their elements

nodes.summary: For any two lists $L$ and $R$ of binomial trees over a linearly ordered type, the multiset of elements of the meld of $L$ and $R$ is the sum of the multisets of elements of $L$ and $R$.
nodes.title: Melding binomial forests adds their elements

nodes.summary: For any two binomial heaps $H_1$ and $H_2$ over a linearly ordered type, the multiset of elements of the meld of $H_1$ and $H_2$ is the sum of the multisets of elements of $H_1$ and $H_2$.
nodes.title: Melding binomial heaps adds their elements

nodes.summary: The multiset of elements of a binomial tree with root value $x$ and children $t_1, \dots, t_k$ is defined recursively as $\{x\}$ added to the multiset sum of the multisets of elements of $t_1, \dots, t_k$; the stored rank plays no role.
nodes.title: Elements of a binomial tree

nodes.summary: For a linearly ordered type $\alpha$, the empty binomial heap over $\alpha$ is the binomial heap whose list of trees is empty.
nodes.title: Empty binomial heap

nodes.summary: For a binomial heap $H$ over a linearly ordered type, the minimum lookup of $H$ returns no value if and only if the list of trees of $H$ is empty.
nodes.title: The minimum lookup fails exactly on the empty binomial heap

nodes.summary: Let $H$ be a binomial heap over a linearly ordered type. If the minimum lookup of $H$ returns $m$, then $m \le v$ for every element $v$ of $H$.
nodes.title: The minimum lookup of a binomial heap returns a lower bound

nodes.summary: Let $H$ be a binomial heap over a linearly ordered type. If the minimum lookup of $H$ returns $m$, then $m$ is an element of $H$.
nodes.title: The minimum lookup of a binomial heap returns one of its elements

nodes.summary: The minimum lookup of a binomial heap over a linearly ordered type returns no value when the heap has no trees, and otherwise returns the least of the root values of its trees, leaving the heap unchanged.
nodes.title: Minimum of a binomial heap

nodes.summary: Inserting a value $x$ into a binomial heap $H$ over a linearly ordered type gives the meld of the one-element binomial heap containing $x$ with $H$.
nodes.title: Insertion into a binomial heap

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a type with a relation $\le$. If a list of binomial trees over $\alpha$ is a valid binomial forest and its multiset of elements has cardinality $0$, then the list has length $0$.
nodes.title: A valid binomial forest with no elements has no trees

nodes.summary: If a binomial heap over a linearly ordered type has $n$ elements, counted with multiplicity, then its number of trees is at most $\lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor + 1$, where $\lfloor \log_2 0 \rfloor$ is taken to be $0$.
nodes.title: A binomial heap has logarithmically many trees

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a type with a relation $\le$. If a valid binomial forest over $\alpha$ has $n$ elements, counted with multiplicity, then it consists of at most $\lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor + 1$ trees, where $\lfloor \log_2 0 \rfloor$ is taken to be $0$.
nodes.title: A valid binomial forest has logarithmically many trees

nodes.summary: If $s$ and $t$ are valid binomial trees of equal rank, then the tree obtained by linking $s$ with $t$ is valid.
nodes.title: Linking preserves binomial-tree validity

nodes.summary: Over a linear order, the link of binomial trees $s$ and $t$ is defined as follows. If the root of $s$ is at most the root of $t$, it is the tree whose rank is one more than the rank of $s$, whose root is the root of $s$, and whose children are $t$ followed by the children of $s$. Otherwise it is the tree whose rank is one more than the rank of $s$, whose root is the root of $t$, and whose children are $s$ followed…
nodes.title: Linking two binomial trees

nodes.summary: Let $r$ be a natural number and let $F$ and $G$ be valid binomial forests in which every tree has rank at least $r$. Then the meld of $F$ and $G$ is a valid binomial forest in which every tree has rank at least $r$.
nodes.title: Melding preserves forest validity and rank lower bounds

nodes.summary: Over a linear order, the meld of two lists of binomial trees is defined by recursion on their total length. For every list $L$, the meld of the empty list with $L$ is $L$, and the meld of $L$ with the empty list is $L$. For nonempty lists with first trees $s$ and $t$ and remaining lists $F$ and $G$: if the rank of $s$ is less than the rank of $t$, the meld is $s$ followed by the meld of $F$ with the second list; if…
nodes.title: Melding binomial forests

nodes.summary: Over a linear order, the meld of two binomial heaps is the binomial heap whose forest is the meld of the forests of the two heaps.
nodes.title: Melding binomial heaps

nodes.summary: If $F$ is a valid binomial forest and $T$ is a tree of $F$ of rank $r$, then $r \le \lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor$, where $n$ is the number of elements, counted with multiplicity, represented by $F$.
nodes.title: Tree ranks in a valid forest are logarithmic

nodes.summary: Every tree in a binomial heap holding $n$ elements, counted with multiplicity, has rank at most $\lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor$.
nodes.title: Tree ranks in a binomial heap are logarithmic

nodes.summary: A valid binomial tree of rank $r$ holding $n$ elements, counted with multiplicity, satisfies $r \le \lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor$.
nodes.title: The rank of a valid binomial tree is logarithmic

nodes.summary: The rank of a binomial tree is the natural number stored at its root node.
nodes.title: Rank of a binomial tree

nodes.summary: For a natural number $r$, a list of binomial trees has ranks at least $r$ when every tree in it has rank at least $r$.
nodes.title: Rank lower bound for a forest

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a list of binomial trees over a linear order, and suppose that removing a minimum tree from $T$ returns the tree $m$ and the list $R$. Then the multiset represented by $m$ plus the multiset represented by the forest $R$ equals the multiset represented by the forest $T$; $m$ is a member of $T$; $R$ is a sublist of $T$; and the root of $m$ is at most the root of every tree in $T$.
nodes.title: Removing a minimum-root tree

nodes.summary: For a list $T$ of binomial trees over a linear order, the result is nothing when $T$ is empty. Otherwise it is the first tree $m$ of $T$ whose root is minimal among the roots of the trees of $T$, together with the list obtained from $T$ by deleting that occurrence of $m$, the remaining trees keeping their order.
nodes.title: Removing a minimum-root tree from a forest

nodes.summary: For a type $\alpha$ with a relation $\le$ and a valid binomial tree $t$ over $\alpha$, the root $a$ of $t$ satisfies $a \le v$ for every element $v$ of the multiset represented by $t$.
nodes.title: The root of a valid binomial tree is a lower bound

nodes.summary: For every binomial tree $t$, the root of $t$ occurs in the multiset represented by $t$.
nodes.title: The root of a binomial tree is one of its elements

nodes.summary: The root of the binomial tree with rank $r$, root value $a$ and list of children $c$ is $a$.
nodes.title: Root of a binomial tree

nodes.summary: For a value $a$ in a linearly ordered type $\alpha$, the one-element binomial heap of $a$ is the binomial heap whose list of trees consists of exactly one tree: the binomial tree of rank $0$ with root $a$ and no children.
nodes.title: One-element binomial heap

nodes.summary: For a value $a$ in a linear order, the binomial heap whose list of trees consists of exactly one tree: the tree of rank $0$ with root $a$ and no children.
nodes.title: Singleton binomial heap

nodes.summary: For a type $\alpha$ with a relation $\le$ and lists $L$, $R$ of binomial trees over $\alpha$, if $L$ is a sublist of $R$ (obtained by deleting entries while keeping the order of the rest) and $R$ is a valid forest, then $L$ is a valid forest.
nodes.title: Validity of binomial forests passes to sublists

nodes.summary: For a type $\alpha$ with a relation $\le$, a list of binomial trees over $\alpha$ is a valid forest when every tree in it is a valid binomial tree and the ranks of its trees are strictly increasing along the list.
nodes.title: Valid binomial forest

nodes.summary: For every type $\alpha$ with a relation $\le$, the empty list of binomial trees over $\alpha$ is a valid binomial forest.
nodes.title: The empty forest is valid

nodes.summary: For a linearly ordered type $\alpha$ and a valid binomial tree $t$ over $\alpha$, the children of $t$ listed in reverse order form a valid binomial forest: every tree in the list is valid and the ranks strictly increase along the list.
nodes.title: Reversed children of a valid binomial tree form a valid forest

nodes.summary: For a linearly ordered type $\alpha$ and any $a \in \alpha$, the singleton binomial tree with rank $0$, root $a$ and no children is valid.
nodes.title: Singleton binomial trees are valid

nodes.summary: For a type $\alpha$ with a relation $\le$, validity of binomial trees over $\alpha$ is defined inductively: the tree with stored rank $r$, root $a$ and list of children $c_1, \dots, c_k$ is valid when every child $c_i$ is valid, the ranks of $c_1, \dots, c_k$ are exactly $r - 1, r - 2, \dots, 0$ in this order, the multiset of elements of the tree (its root together with the elements of all its children) has exactly…
nodes.title: Valid binomial tree

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
